extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/agents, USPTO OED staff, disciplinary counsel, and attorneys subject to USPTO reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards the USPTO applies when considering and imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24, including notice, opportunity to respond, publication, and operational consequences of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state court under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of OED may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and the OED Director must send a Notice and Order to the respondent, providing an opportunity to file a response within 40 days opposing imposition of identical discipline based on the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (service and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be served with a Notice and Order and given 40 days to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt provided) and delivered on a specified date; failure to file a response within the 40-day period is material to the USPTO's determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may oppose reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more of the grounds listed in § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order explicitly informs the respondent that opposition must be based on one or more reasons in § 11.24(d)(1); the order finds no response was filed, so no genuine issue of material fact exists under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent fails to respond to the Notice and Order, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states that in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and suspension for three years is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary predicate: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline can be predicated upon violation of § 11.804(h) when the respondent was suspended by a duly constituted state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order suspends Respondent for three years for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended for three years by the Supreme Court of Missouri.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court misconduct findings as basis for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of professional misconduct by a state supreme court (including specific Rules of Professional Conduct violations) can serve as the factual predicate for USPTO reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order reproduces Missouri's findings: violations of Rules 4-5.5(e) (unauthorized practice of law while suspended/failing CLE), 4-8.4(c) and 4-8.4(d) (practicing law while suspended and failing to notify employer/clients), and 4-8.1(c) (knowingly failing to respond to a lawful demand from a disciplinary authority). These state findings underlie USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO disciplinary actions are taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority including 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the legal bases for imposing reciprocal discipline and directing publication/notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of suspension notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension and the grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs the OED Director to publish a specific Notice of Suspension containing respondent's name, registration number, nature and length of the suspension, and that it was predicated upon being suspended by a state authority for violating § 11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, and to courts where respondent is known to be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts of admission, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order imposes compliance with § 11.58 duties as a condition of the suspension (the order does not recite the duties' text but directs compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of respondent from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and associated public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs the USPTO to dissociate Respondent's name from Customer Numbers and the PKI certificate associated with those numbers as part of the suspension's operational effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on obtaining or being added to Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or be added to any USPTO Customer Number until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly bars the respondent from applying for or being included in Customer Numbers or obtaining PKI access unless and until reinstatement occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of reciprocal proceedings by OED Director filing a Complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director initiates reciprocal discipline by filing a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order records that the OED Director filed a Complaint requesting imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA reading room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are made publicly available through OED's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order provides a URL and directs that disciplinary decisions can be reviewed at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (public disclosure practice).
